core_obligations: Reduce smoothness to formal smoothness and the first-order lifting problem
Apply the picard-group-first-order-thickening lemma to reduce to H^2(X, I) = 0

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce smoothness to formal smoothness and the first-order lifting problem
Apply the picard-group-first-order-thickening lemma to reduce to H^2(X, I) = 0
Kill H^2 via the dimension bound on R^p f_* I and affineness of T

difficulty_reason: Prove Picardstack_{X/B} -> B is smooth when f has relative dimension <= 1: local finite presentation is known, so formal smoothness suffices; reduce to lifting an invertible module across a first-order thickening X subset X' (base change of T subset T'); the picard-group-first-order-thickening lemma reduces the lift to H^2(X, I) = 0 for the quasi-coherent ideal I cutting out X in X'; R^p f_* I = 0 for p > 1 by the fibre-dimension bound on higher direct images, and H^2(X, I) = H^0(T, R^2 f_* I) vanishes because T is affine.
